title: RAG architecture, two lanes
hook: Naive, hybrid, reranking, query rewriting, graph and agentic RAG. When each one earns its place.
inPlainWords: RAG has two lanes. One is a prepare-once lane that turns your documents into a searchable library. The other runs for every question: find the right pages, then let the model write the answer from them.

useCase.title: A help center with 5,000 articles, product codes and tables
useCase.story: Customers ask things like "Will the XR-2040-B charger work with the 2024 tablet?" The articles contain exact product codes and compatibility tables.

approaches.name: Naive RAG
approaches.what: Turn text into meaning-numbers (embeddings) and fetch the three most similar chunks.
approaches.greatWhen: A prototype on clean, small documents.
approaches.example: It finds articles about chargers in general, but misses the exact code.

approaches.name: Hybrid search
approaches.what: Run a keyword search and a meaning search together, then merge the results.
approaches.greatWhen: Product codes, names and jargon mixed with natural questions.
approaches.example: Keywords catch "XR-2040-B" and meaning catches "works with tablets".

approaches.name: Reranking
approaches.what: A second, more careful pass reorders the top 20 results so the best five go to the model.
approaches.greatWhen: Results are relevant but poorly ordered.
approaches.avoidWhen: The time budget is razor thin.
approaches.example: The compatibility table jumps from ninth place to first.

approaches.name: Query rewriting
approaches.what: Clean up or split the question before searching.
approaches.example: "Does it work with the new one?" becomes "XR-2040-B compatible with 2024 tablet".

approaches.name: Graph RAG
approaches.what: Store relationships, like product to accessory to compatible device, and search along them.
approaches.greatWhen: Questions about connections that span many documents.
approaches.avoidWhen: Simple lookups. It is heavy to build.
approaches.example: "Which accessories work with everything in the Starter Bundle?"

approaches.name: Agentic RAG
approaches.what: The model decides what to search, reads the results, and searches again.
approaches.greatWhen: Multi-step questions that need several lookups.
approaches.avoidWhen: Simple questions. It is slower and costlier.
approaches.example: Compare three products across three documents.

challenge.question: Users ask about exact product codes and also in natural language. What is the best RAG setup?

options.why: A fine baseline, but it can miss exact codes.

options.text: Hybrid search, then reranking, with cited sources
options.why: Keywords catch exact codes, meaning catches the intent, the reranker orders them, and citations let people check.
It is heavy to build for what is really a lookup problem.
Powerful, but slower and costlier. Keep it for multi-step questions.

bestCase.title: Hybrid search, reranking, and cited sources
bestCase.example: "Will XR-2040-B work with the 2024 tablet?" Keyword search catches the exact code, meaning search catches "compatible with tablets", the reranker puts the compatibility table first, and the answer links the table.

worstCase.title: Naive chunks, no citations, no testing
worstCase.example: The table was cut in half, so "Compatible: Yes" sits apart from its header. Search returns the XR-2040-A article. The bot answers confidently about the wrong product, and with no citation nobody notices until a customer complains.

steps.label: Split into chunks
steps.goes: Cut by headings, with tables kept whole.
steps.goesWrong: Cut every 500 characters. The table header and its "Yes" land in different chunks.

steps.label: Two indexes
steps.goes: Stored in a keyword index and a meaning index.

steps.label: Hybrid search
steps.goes: Finds 20 candidates using both kinds of search.

steps.label: Rerank
steps.goes: A careful second look keeps the best five.

steps.label: Model writes
steps.goes: "Answer only from these passages, and cite them."

steps.label: Answer and sources
steps.goes: Yes, compatible. See the compatibility table.

takeaway: RAG quality depends at least as much on the search side (chunking, hybrid, reranking) as on the model.
